methodological_rigor.justification: Small retrospective single-center study (N=60) comparing vascular management approaches in retroperitoneal leiomyosarcoma. Simple chi-squared tests without adjustment for confounding. Three groups: IVC ligation (n=10), IVC replacement (n=36), patch angioplasty (n=14). 43.3% experienced adverse events overall. No statistically significant differences found by group. Limited sample size, no multivariate analysis, no adjustment for case complexity or patient factors.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Addresses surgical approach to vascular involvement in rare tumor (retroperitoneal leiomyosarcoma), relevant to surgical decision-making. However, negative findings (no significant differences by approach) limit clinical impact. LoE very low given retrospective design, small sample, and rare disease. Limited generalizability.

reporting_quality.justification: Basic description of patient groups and outcomes. Results presented as simple counts and percentages. Chi-squared test mentioned but no confidence intervals or detailed statistical reporting. No explicit STROBE adherence. Data and code availability not mentioned. Minimal methodological detail.

novelty_literature.justification: Vascular management strategies in sarcoma surgery previously described. Study documents institutional series without novel approaches or insights. Null findings (no differences between approaches) provide limited new knowledge. Minimal contribution to literature.

writing_presentation.justification: Readable presentation with clear summary of different vascular management approaches. Methods section brief; results straightforward but limited to percentages. Discussion appropriately emphasizes lack of significant differences but offers little insight into why outcomes were similar. Limited depth.

key_strengths: Addresses surgical management of rare tumor subtype (retroperitoneal leiomyosarcoma with vascular involvement)
Negative finding (no significant differences by vascular approach) useful if rigorously demonstrated
Clear presentation of three management strategies
key_concerns: Very small sample size (N=60 total, unequal groups: 10, 36, 14) limits statistical power and precision
Retrospective single-center design with no adjustment for case complexity, surgeon experience, or patient factors
Simple descriptive statistics without multivariate analysis; no confidence intervals provided
Null findings may reflect underpowering rather than true equivalence of approaches
Minimal novelty; little new knowledge contributed by study
No proposed next steps or mechanistic understanding despite null findings
chief_reviewer.rationale: Low-evidence, small retrospective study with null findings in rare disease setting. Insufficient statistical power and methodological rigor. Not suitable for publication at this quality level; would benefit from prospective multicenter design with larger sample and detailed case-complexity adjustment.
